Circulation holds at around 38 lakh copies

Print circulation was about 37.68 lakh copies, essentially unchanged versus the previous quarter and near the post-COVID recovered base. Management is focused on sustaining volumes in core territories and defending share in peripheral markets, even as a modest reduction of roughly 30,000 copies weighed on publishing revenue.

Sectoral ad trends: jewelry, BFSI, healthcare shine

Advertising performance varied sharply by sector, with jewelry and banking and financial services posting solid numbers despite the festive-shift drag. Healthcare delivered strong double-digit growth and IPO advertising jumped about 50% year-on-year, although management highlighted that the absolute IPO volume remained modest in the quarter.

Digital pricing experiments deliver early positive signals

On the digital side, DB Corp. is experimenting with higher app subscription prices, testing an increase from INR 149 to INR 199 across roughly one lakh users. Early feedback has been described as “pretty decent and good,” but management cautioned that it is still too early to quantify the full revenue or churn impact from these pricing experiments.

Election-driven digital push in Uttar Pradesh

Ahead of the upcoming U.P. elections, the company is leaning on its large journalist network and deep ground reporting to sharpen its digital election coverage. Management hopes that higher engagement during the campaign will translate into a larger U.P. subscriber base, leveraging sizeable existing monthly and daily active user pools in the state.

Continued investment in digital despite near-term drag

DB Corp. reiterated its commitment to its digital business, continuing to invest in content, technology, and experimentation even as monetization remains nascent. The company is running multiple tests across subscriptions, advertising formats, and partnerships, and believes the strategic direction over the last two years has been broadly positive.

Three-pronged digital monetization model taking shape

Management is deliberately building a diversified digital revenue model based on advertising, subscriptions, and technology tie-ups rather than relying on a single stream. App advertising, introduced only about four quarters ago, is still in test mode as the company seeks to balance monetization with user experience and avoid cluttering the product.

Cost discipline offsets some margin pressure

Operating costs other than newsprint remained under control, with personnel and overhead expenses tightly managed and cuts taken across most cost lines. Quarter-on-quarter increases in some cost heads were mainly tied to sales-driven events, which management said generated corresponding revenue and profits, helping protect margins.

Robust cash pile and light capex needs

The balance sheet remains strong with around INR 1,120 crore in cash and bank balances and no major capex plans in the near term, as key printing and production assets are already in place. Management does not foresee significant capital expenditure over the next few quarters, creating optionality for future shareholder distributions or strategic deployment.

Capital allocation: interim dividend paid, more under review

An interim dividend of INR 5 per share was already paid in Q1, signaling a willingness to return cash to investors. The board is now evaluating options for further distribution of surplus cash to stakeholders, keeping in mind business needs, investment in digital, and the external environment.

Lease termination boosts other income

The redevelopment of the company’s registered office building in Ahmedabad led to the termination of its lease and derecognition of the related right-of-use asset and liability. This accounting adjustment generated other income of roughly INR 13.39 crore under applicable accounting standards, supporting reported profitability in the quarter.

Cover prices kept flat to protect circulation

Management has consciously avoided raising newspaper cover prices, arguing that higher prices could accelerate circulation declines in a still-sensitive readership base. The strategic priority is to keep print products affordable and stabilize or gently grow circulation, even if it means forgoing some near-term pricing upside.

Festive shift skews quarterly comparability

An eight-day shift of the key festive period from September to October pushed an estimated INR 40 crore of advertising revenue into Q3, making this quarter’s numbers a poor like-for-like comparison. With Navratri falling in Q3 this year, management emphasized that investors should assess performance over the half-year rather than a single distorted quarter.

Macro, weather and election clouds over ad demand

Management flagged geopolitical tensions, heavy rains in certain regions such as Rajasthan, and election-related codes of conduct as factors weighing on government and private advertising. Panchayat elections in some states caused a temporary drop in government campaigns, while the potential uplift from election advertising, including U.P., is still uncertain.

Circulation plateau and its revenue impact

After recovering most of the COVID-era circulation losses, DB Corp. has struggled to grow beyond this restored base, with only small percentage swings quarter to quarter. A fall of about 30,000 copies contributed to publishing revenue slipping from INR 120 crore to INR 116 crore, underlining how sensitive print revenues remain to even minor volume changes.

Newsprint inflation squeezes margins

Average newsprint costs surged about 20.8% year-on-year to roughly INR 57,000 per ton, driven by geopolitical disruptions, higher imported prices, domestic follow-through, and elevated freight. Management expects only a modest 2%-3% price easing in Q3 and Q4, leaving an 18%-20% cost headwind versus last year and limiting near-term margin relief.

Tight newsprint supply limits pricing power

With newsprint supply still tight, securing adequate volumes has taken priority over negotiating lower rates, reducing DB Corp.’s leverage with suppliers. The company anticipates only marginal price declines even as comparisons remain tough, implying continued pressure on print profitability until global supply conditions ease more meaningfully.

Digital MAUs soften amid lower marketing spend

Digital monthly active users slipped from around 20 million in Q4 to 18 million in Q2, a move management framed as a 3%-4% fluctuation across quarters. The decline was partly attributed to reduced marketing expenditure and partly to ongoing experimentation with subscriber value propositions, as the company tests different pricing and engagement levers.

Digital ad market visibility still low

The digital advertising backdrop remains murky, with inventory increasing across platforms while DB Corp. positions itself as a premium rather than commoditized player. The company has expanded its digital team, but also saw some exits due to a mismatch between expectation and delivery, underscoring execution challenges in this evolving segment.

Monetization metrics remain early-stage

Management reiterated that all three digital revenue pillars—advertising, subscriptions, and tech alliances—are still at a nascent stage, with experiments ongoing. Because of this early phase, the company is not yet ready to share hard data on revenue uplift from the recent subscription price hikes, preferring to wait for more evidence.

Mixed advertising performance across key sectors

Sectorally, FMCG advertising was down about 2%, lifestyle and hypermarkets were weaker and automobiles remained flat, reflecting a patchy consumer backdrop. Real estate and education posted single-digit growth, with management noting that real estate likely would have delivered double-digit growth had the festive season remained in the reported quarter.

Limited digital disclosure amid competitive concerns

DB Corp. is cautious about releasing granular digital data, citing prior investor approval to withhold detailed metrics in a competitive environment. The request for more transparency on historical and forward digital trends will be taken to the board, suggesting that any step-up in disclosure will be a considered strategic decision.

Guidance: ad growth ambitions amid cost overhang

Looking ahead, management expects the festive shift to add roughly INR 40 crore of advertising in Q3 and remains “pretty optimistic” about the next two quarters, targeting high single-digit to early double-digit ad revenue growth for the year. Newsprint costs are seen easing only 2%-3% in Q3 and Q4, circulation should stay around 38 lakh copies, digital pricing tests will continue, key ad verticals such as healthcare and IPOs are expected to stay strong, and no major capex is planned over the next several quarters, supported by around INR 1,120 crore of cash.

DB Corp.’s earnings call painted a picture of a resilient print franchise navigating cost inflation and structural digital shifts with cautious confidence. For investors, the key watchpoints will be festive and election-driven ad traction, the pace of digital monetization, and any easing in newsprint costs, all set against the backdrop of a strong balance sheet and disciplined capital allocation.

data.title: LTIMindtree Earnings Call: AI-Fueled Growth Amid Headwinds
data.description:
LTIMindtree Limited ((IN:LTIM)) has held its Q2 earnings call. Read on for the main highlights of the call.

LTIMindtree’s latest earnings call struck a cautiously optimistic tone, with management leaning on broad-based revenue growth, a firmer EBIT margin, and surging AI revenues to argue that the worst of the slowdown is past. Yet investors were also reminded of softer PAT margins, weak cash conversion, Middle East headwinds, and persistent pricing pressure in traditional IT services.

Broad-Based Revenue Growth and Margin Resilience

Revenue for Q2 FY 2027 reached $1.235 billion, up 1.1% quarter-on-quarter and 5.1% year-on-year in constant currency, with INR revenue climbing 13.6% year-on-year. EBIT margin edged up 10 basis points sequentially to 15.6%, and management reiterated its ambition to keep full-year margins broadly in line with last year while nudging organic profitability higher.

Promotion

55% Off TipRanks

  • Unlock powerful investing tools with TipRanks Premium to make smarter, more confident investment decisions
  • Subscribe to TipRanks Smart Investor Newsletter, and discover new investing opportunities with data-backed stock picks
Learn more about TipRanks Premium

AI Revenue Becomes a Core Growth Engine

AI revenue, including enterprise AI, surged to 13.4% of total revenue and grew 40% year-on-year, with cumulative AI revenue up 47%. Management emphasized that AI rate cards sit above traditional pricing and that AI work carries a better gross margin profile, suggesting a structural tailwind for profitability as the AI mix continues to rise.

AI-Led Deal Flow and Pipeline Health

Total order inflows hit $1.3 billion, driven by AI-centric deals that are shorter cycle, faster to convert into revenue, and largely incremental. While this skews traditional TCV metrics, management stressed that the overall pipeline, including large deals, remains healthy, and that more disclosure on ACV versus TCV will follow as the model stabilizes.

Financial Services and Vertical Diversification

Financial services, a key vertical, grew 3.1% sequentially and returned to positive year-on-year growth at 0.4%, with a client graduating into the $100 million-plus bucket and room for further expansion. Three of four industry segments posted more than 7% year-on-year growth, with tech and services, consumer, and production all contributing to diversification.

Geographic and Client-Category Expansion

Americas revenue increased 1.5% quarter-on-quarter and Europe rose 1%, offsetting softness elsewhere. All client tiers from $5 million to $100 million-plus grew year-on-year, underscoring broader wallet-share gains even as specific regions like the Middle East weighed on short-term performance.

Headcount Growth and AI Skills Upgrade

Total headcount rose to 88,835 with a net addition of 949 employees, including 1,743 freshers, signaling confidence in near-term demand. The AI1000 program is ramping well, with about 1,000 employees in specialized AI learning journeys and more than 2,000 certifications across leading AI platforms such as Claude, Gemini, Copilot, and Azure AI.

Sales Enablement and Shifting AI Demand

A global AI-focused sales enablement program has been completed, equipping sales teams to pitch and shape end-to-end AI solutions. Management highlighted that client demand is moving from pilots to deployment, focusing on business-process redesign, contextual implementations, data sovereignty, and economic optimization through AI.

BlueVerse Platform and Ecosystem Expansion

The BlueVerse ecosystem continued to broaden across AI foundry services, data modernization, AI-led engineering, domain-specific small language models, and governance. New offerings such as BlueVerse OneToken, WriteLogic, Sovereign Few, additional domain small language models, and six AI patents underscore LTIMindtree’s platform-first approach.

Strategic AI Partnerships and New Facilities

LTIMindtree embedded Claude and Claude Code into BlueVerse via an Anthropic tie-up and partnered with Glean to fuse enterprise knowledge with BlueVerse, while teaming with Cognition to bring Devin into WriteLogic. Collaborations with IBM, Red Hat, Chainguard, and others on AI and software-supply-chain security, plus new AI centers in Kolkata and Hyderabad, deepen delivery capabilities.

Proven AI Outcomes for Clients

Management showcased concrete AI benefits, including 100% classification across more than 18 failure scenarios for an agentic recovery platform and a fintech case with 50% lower delivery cycle time and a 38% cut in development effort. Other examples ranged from potential 40% HR ticket reduction to 50% productivity gains and materially faster modeling in marketing and operations use cases.

External Validation and ESG Credentials

BlueVerse bagged a Gold Stevie Award and recognition at the Times of India AI Quotient Awards, while LTIMindtree earned ISG Paragon Awards and leadership positions in ISG’s U.S. Microsoft AI and Cloud Ecosystem quadrants. Strong ESG scores from local rating bodies, alongside other HR and knowledge awards, add non-financial credibility that may appeal to long-term investors.

Working Capital, Cash, and Shareholder Returns

Working capital efficiency ticked up as DSO improved by one day to 84, and cash plus investments stood at about $1.6 billion. The board raised the interim dividend to INR 25 per share, up 13.6% year-on-year, while reiterating a capital-allocation stance that balances 40%-45% payouts with investment in M&A, AI platforms, talent, and GCC capabilities.

Randstad Acquisition and Inorganic Growth

Regulatory approvals for acquiring parts of Randstad’s digital businesses in Europe and Australia remain on schedule, with closure targeted in Q3 FY 2027. Management expects three to four months post-close to realign these new markets, using them as beachheads to deepen presence and cross-sell LTIMindtree’s broader digital and AI offerings.

Profitability Headwinds and Cash Conversion Dip

PAT margin slipped to 11.7% from 12.7% as the prior quarter benefited from a one-off gain on an AI investment, pushing basic EPS down to INR 47.2 from INR 49.5. Operating cash flow to PAT fell sharply to 39%, and free cash flow to PAT to 24%, due to advance payments, gratuity-related funding, dividend tax withholding, and higher advance taxes.

Return Ratios and Capital Efficiency

Return on capital employed softened to 28.5% from 29.8% as lower PAT and cash conversion weighed on capital productivity. Management argued that the current investment cycle in AI capabilities, M&A, and new markets is necessary to sustain growth and margins, even if it temporarily caps improvements in return metrics.

Regional Weakness and Tech Segment Volatility

Tech and services revenue fell 4% sequentially, hurt by seasonal renewal cycles and a sharp slowdown in Saudi Arabia, which is booked within the tech segment through a joint venture. Rest-of-world revenue declined 1.4% quarter-on-quarter as the broader Middle East business saw a material absolute revenue impact from factors described as outside the company’s control.

Consumer and Travel Under Pressure

Consumer revenue managed just 0.3% sequential growth, and travel and hospitality clients pulled back amid higher fuel and energy costs and associated macro uncertainty. These customers are becoming more selective, focusing spending on critical projects and postponing discretionary work, which adds short-term drag to bookings and revenue.

Deal Mix, TCV Visibility, and Pricing Pressure

The quarter’s deal inflows leaned toward shorter-duration, AI-led engagements, making traditional TCV less meaningful and spotlighting ACV as a better metric, which management plans to detail in coming quarters. At the same time, large traditional deals face fierce price competition, with unit pricing declining and productivity gains and AI infusion pressuring legacy revenue pools.

Productivity Deflation and Traditional Services Outlook

LTIMindtree estimates it has passed through about 60% of total productivity headwinds to clients, with 60%-70% of its portfolio already re-based and 20%-30% still to be reset through renewal, consolidation, or AI-driven transformation. Management expects industry-wide pricing and productivity pressure in traditional services to persist for a couple of years as automation and AI adoption deepen.

CBDT Ramp-Up and Hardware Constraints

Revenue growth in the CBDT business remains tied to the availability and pricing of hardware, which weighed on the ramp in recent quarters. Conditions have improved compared with Q1, and management expects a gradual volume build-up as supply normalizes, providing a modest tailwind to growth without significantly altering the margin profile.

Forex and Gratuity-Related Drags

Below-EBIT foreign-exchange losses are likely to persist for the next few quarters and could increase if the rupee weakens, though that would simultaneously lift rupee-reported business profitability. A small residual cash outflow is expected from gratuity funding in the next quarter, and while cash conversion should improve, management cautioned that prior peak levels may not immediately return.

Forward-Looking Guidance and Margin Ambition

Management pointed to 5.4% year-on-year growth in the first half and reiterated that H2 should outpace H1, with Q3 and Q4 set to be better than Q1 as the growth trajectory strengthens. The aim is to get FY 2027 growth as close as possible to FY 2026, keep EBIT margins broadly similar to last year while gently improving organic margins, and position the business for a stronger FY 2028 as Randstad integration, CBDT ramp-up, tech recovery, and normalized cash flows take hold.

LTIMindtree’s earnings call paints the picture of a company leaning hard into AI and platforms to offset cyclical and structural headwinds in legacy services and select geographies. Investors will watch whether the promised second-half acceleration, AI-led margin uplift, and improving cash conversion materialize, but the strategic direction and execution on AI capabilities give the story a constructive medium-term bias.

data.description:
Metro Brands Ltd. ((IN:METROBRAND)) has held its Q2 earnings call. Read on for the main highlights of the call.

Metro Brands’ latest earnings call struck a broadly upbeat tone, with management highlighting double-digit growth in revenue, EBITDA and profit, healthier gross margins and solid traction in e-commerce. Executives acknowledged cost and inventory pressures and uneven performance in some newer formats, but stressed disciplined expansion and a medium- to long-term horizon for scaling brands like Clarks, Crocs and FILA.

Strong Q2 Standalone Financial Performance

Second-quarter standalone net sales rose 12% year-on-year to INR 712 crore, underscoring resilient demand in the core business despite cost headwinds. Profit after tax climbed 14% to INR 73 crore, while EBITDA grew 15%, signaling good operating leverage even as the company continued to invest in newer formats and capabilities.

Promotion

  • Unlock powerful investing tools with TipRanks Premium to make smarter, more confident investment decisions
  • Subscribe to TipRanks Smart Investor Newsletter, and discover new investing opportunities with data-backed stock picks
Learn more about TipRanks Premium

Consolidated Revenue and EBITDA Growth

On a consolidated basis, Q2 revenue increased 12.2% to INR 730 crore, supported by growth across formats and channels. EBITDA jumped 15.9% to INR 198 crore and margin improved to 27.1% from 26.2%, while consolidated PAT advanced about 12% to INR 77 crore with a stable 10.6% margin, reflecting controlled costs despite some pressure below gross profit.

E-Commerce and Omni-Channel Expansion

Digital channels remained a key growth driver, with e-commerce and omni-channel sales up 12% in Q2 and contributing 14.2% of revenue. For the first half, online sales grew 11% and formed 13.6% of revenue, as Metro Brands continued to connect stores with marketplaces and leaned into emerging AI-driven discovery platforms to keep its brands visible and convenient for consumers.

Improved Gross Margin

The first half saw gross margin rise to 58.4% from 57.3% a year earlier, aided by lower average discounts on end-of-season and online sales and slightly better markups. A modestly lower contribution from e-commerce, which tends to carry higher discounting, also supported the improvement, although management cautioned that some of these gains are not fully sustainable quarter to quarter.

Festive Demand Shift Supports Q3 Opportunity

Metro Brands flagged a favorable demand shift, with a larger portion of festive buying moving into Q3 as the calendar pushed key events from September to October. Durga Puja was described as having performed very well, and other markets also showed strength on a like-for-like basis, giving management confidence in Q3 momentum as the company focuses on capturing festive footfall.

Store Network Expansion

The retailer continued to expand its footprint, opening 21 stores and closing nine in Q2 for a net addition of 12 outlets. In the first half it opened 34 stores and closed 13, taking the network to 1,053 stores at the end of September, reflecting a balance between growth and pruning underperforming locations.

Disciplined and Selective Store Expansion

Management emphasized that expansion will be selective, prioritizing profitability over hitting a headline store count. Store-opening criteria have been tightened amid high rentals and constrained real-estate supply, with H2 additions expected to exceed H1 but closures likely to remain around 2%-3%, consistent with historical levels and a focus on network quality.

Established Own Brands Remain the Core Business

Metro, Mochi and Walkway continued to anchor the portfolio, with own brands contributing about 70% of store product sales in the first half. Management argued these proprietary labels provide a strong foundation for margins and customer loyalty, complementing international partnerships and the multi-brand platform that diversify the company’s offering.

Clarks Distribution and Store Opportunity

Clarks is emerging as a key growth vector, with women’s products now present in more than 400 multi-brand outlets and a limited men’s range in over 100. The full assortment is already available on the direct-to-consumer site, and a complete exclusive-store range is slated for Q3, ahead of a planned rollout of Clarks exclusive stores once supply-chain and assortment are fully stabilized.

Positive Clarks Supply Chain and Consumer Response

Management described Clarks’ supply chain as nimble and robust, with most production localized in India and no carryover-inventory or regulatory complications. Consumer response has been “extremely high and rapid,” suggesting the brand could scale quickly once the assortment is complete, providing a meaningful incremental growth lever for Metro Brands.

Crocs Continues to Grow

Crocs remained a strong contributor, continuing to grow despite a high base built over the last few years and still accounting for less than 20% of overall business. Management noted that selective openings of Crocs-owned stores in high-heat markets may create a halo effect that benefits Metro’s sales, reinforcing the value of the partnership.

Walkway Existing-Store Productivity Improvement

Walkway, the value-focused format, is showing early signs of improvement, with like-for-like productivity gains emerging in existing stores. Metro Brands has opened more than 35 Walkway stores in the past 12-14 months on a base of around 60-70, and is now using performance data from these locations to refine its new-store formula before accelerating expansion.

Geographic Mix Remains Broadly Consistent

The company’s geographic footprint remains diversified, with roughly 31% of business from the West and 33% from the South. Management said store-to-sales contribution has stayed broadly consistent, even as metro cities have begun to slightly over-index in performance, despite a greater number of new stores opening in lower-tier markets.

Positive Medium-Term Margin Framework

Metro Brands reiterated a constructive margin outlook, expecting H2 PAT to beat H1 in line with historical seasonality and the festive demand shift. The company views a 15% PAT margin as medium- to long-term guidance, targeting a sustainable range of 13%-15% as newer businesses scale and begin contributing more meaningfully to profits.

Marketing and Capability Investment

First-half marketing spend increased to about 4% of revenue from roughly 3.25%-3.4% last year, reflecting stepped-up investment behind incubating new brands. Management expects marketing intensity to stay around 4%, while also allocating capital to talent, brand building and newer formats that are seen as crucial for long-term growth and competitive differentiation.

Planned Capital Expenditure

CapEx plans for FY 2027 and FY 2028 were pegged at around INR 80 crore-INR 100 crore annually, including store remodels to refresh the existing network. Management described roughly INR 100 crore as a reasonable level of investment to support store modernization and measured expansion without over-leveraging the balance sheet.

Frontline Compensation Changes Intended to Support Talent

To stay competitive in the retail labor market, Metro Brands plans to revise remuneration for store teams and keep pay well above minimum wage levels in most states. Front-end staff costs are expected to rise by 0.5%-1%, an increase management views as an investment in attracting and retaining talent, improving service standards and driving sales growth over time.

FILA Repositioning and Local Manufacturing

FILA is undergoing a strategic overhaul, including the start of local footwear manufacturing in India to address regulatory-related supply concerns. The repositioning focuses on sharper merchandise and pricing, with the transformation expected to unfold over the next 12-18 months before store expansion picks up from FY 2028, supported by a medium-term ambition to scale store counts significantly.

Costs Offset Part of Gross Margin Improvement

While gross margin improved, several cost lines diluted the benefit further down the income statement, including ongoing talent and brand-building investments. Higher frontline staff costs after minimum-wage revisions, modest occupancy-cost increases linked to new formats and lower treasury income versus a strong prior year all weighed on the bottom line.

Rental and Operating Cost Pressure

Management openly acknowledged rental pressure, noting that higher real-estate costs are driving negative operating leverage in some locations. Additional headwinds included front-end staff-cost inflation, continued salary investments and elevated marketing spend, all of which are deemed necessary but have short-term impact on profitability metrics.

PAT Margin Below the 15% Long-Term Target in H1

First-half PAT margin fell short of the roughly 15% level discussed with analysts, reflecting the combination of cost pressures and lower treasury gains. Management reiterated that H2 should be better than H1 and framed 15% PAT as a medium- to long-term objective, with a more realistic near-term range around 13%-15% as newer businesses mature.

Inventory Remains Elevated

Inventory levels were described as higher than desired, driven by front-loaded purchases ahead of expected raw-material cost increases and stock built for brands such as FitFlop, Clarks and Foot Locker. Management aims to normalize inventory by March, targeting around 80 working-capital days by mid to end of the next financial year and viewing about seven months of stock as the ideal level.

Store Additions Were Lower in H1

H1 saw net additions of 21 stores, with 34 openings and 13 closures, a slower pace than some investors may expect. Management attributed the moderation to tighter store-opening filters amid elevated rentals and constrained high-quality real-estate supply, but signaled that H2 additions should improve while still favoring quality over quantity.

BIS-Related Supply Uncertainty

Regulatory implementation has created supply uncertainty for selected external brands, affecting timing and readiness for formats like Foot Locker and MetroActiv. Management also highlighted higher risk for Foot Locker and FitFlop due to import dependence, noting that several growth brands still face some exposure to these rules and that expansion is being calibrated accordingly.

FILA Supply and Repositioning Challenges

FILA faced meaningful disruption, including supply interruptions, elevated old-inventory levels and the need to build new product-development capabilities for athletic footwear. These challenges forced Metro Brands to craft new product architecture, design and brand language, creating near-term drag as the company experiments and learns the right approach for the segment.

Foot Locker and MetroActiv Expansion Calibrated to Product Availability

For Foot Locker and MetroActiv, store opening plans are tightly linked to product availability, given the BIS-related supply constraints. Management stressed that capital allocation and expansion will remain aligned with supply readiness and operational progress, avoiding aggressive rollout until assortments and logistics are robust enough to support performance.

Gross-Margin Improvement Is Partly Non-Sustainable

Executives cautioned that a meaningful portion of Q2 gross-margin improvement came from lower end-of-season sale discounts, a benefit unlikely to repeat in Q3. Future margins will also vary with business mix, with formats like Walkway, Foot Locker and MetroActiv potentially exerting downward pressure as their share of sales rises due to their different pricing and discount profiles.

Raw-Material Inflation and Price Increases

The company is contending with raw-material inflation of roughly 10%-15% across its basket, prompting average selling price hikes of about 2%-4%, or slightly more on some articles. These measured increases are intended to offset cost pressures without significantly hurting demand, balancing margin protection with consumer affordability.

New-Store Productivity Still Uneven at Walkway

Walkway’s recent expansion has produced mixed results, with around 30% of new stores performing well, 30% average and 30% described as poor or failures. Management conceded that the optimal new-store formula is not yet fully established and is using this experience to refine location and assortment strategy before scaling the format more aggressively.

Sales-Per-Square-Foot Pressure from Store Openings and Cannibalization

The company noted that new stores typically operate at lower productivity than mature outlets, which weighs on average sales per square foot. Opening additional formats near successful existing stores can also create cannibalization, limiting the flow-through of same-store growth into overall sales density, a dynamic management is now factoring into its expansion plans.

Lower Treasury Income Affected PAT Growth

Other income in the first half was around INR 54 crore versus approximately INR 100 crore for the full prior year, highlighting a tougher comparison. Management said this drop in treasury gains was a significant factor behind relatively muted PAT growth, even as operating metrics like revenue and EBITDA showed healthy double-digit increases.

Forward-Looking Guidance and Strategic Outlook

Looking ahead, Metro Brands expects store closures to stay around 2%-3% and H2 to deliver stronger store additions and better PAT than H1, while aiming for a medium- to long-term PAT margin band of 13%-15%. Staff costs are projected to rise modestly, marketing to remain near 4% of revenue, CapEx around INR 100 crore annually, and inventory to normalize over the next year as transformations in Clarks and FILA steadily progress.

Metro Brands’ earnings call painted the picture of a company balancing strong core performance with cautious investment in newer brands and formats. For investors, the key takeaway is a constructive growth and margin story tempered by cost and regulatory headwinds, with management clearly focused on disciplined expansion, inventory control and building the foundations for multi-brand, omni-channel scale.
